landmarks.name: Iguazu Falls
landmarks.writeup: One of the largest and most spectacular waterfall systems in the world, located on the border with Brazil.

wiki.extract:
Puerto Iguazú is a border city in the province of Misiones, Argentina. With a population of 82,227 ,
it is the fourth largest city in the Province, after Posadas, Oberá, and Eldorado.
The Iguazú Falls are 18 kilometres (11 mi) away from the city, and as a result the city has developed much of its infrastructure around tourism.

landmarks.name: Perito Moreno Glacier
landmarks.writeup: A massive glacier in Patagonia known for its dynamic ice ruptures and stunning blue ice formations.

wiki.extract: The Perito Moreno, Francisco Gormaz or Bismarck Glacier is a glacier located in Los Glaciares National Park in southwest Santa Cruz Province, Argentina, and originated in the Magallanes Region in Chile, being also part of the Bernardo O'Higgins National Park. It is one of the most important tourist attractions in the Argentine Patagonia.

landmarks.name: Casa Rosada
landmarks.writeup: The executive mansion and office of the President of Argentina, located in Buenos Aires.

wiki.extract: The Casa Rosada, lit. 'the pink house', is the president of the Argentine Republic's official workplace, located in Buenos Aires. The palatial mansion is known officially as Casa de Gobierno. Normally, the president lives at the Quinta de Olivos, the president of Argentina's official residence, located in Olivos, Greater Buenos Aires. The characteristic color of the Casa Rosada is baby pink, and it is considered one of the most emblematic buildings in Buenos Aires. The building also houses a museum, which contains objects relating to former presidents of Argentina. It has been declared a National Historic Monument of Argentina.

landmarks.name: La Boca
landmarks.writeup: A colorful neighborhood in Buenos Aires famous for its vibrant street art and tango culture.

wiki.extract: La Boca is a neighborhood (barrio) of Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina.

landmarks.name: Aconcagua
landmarks.writeup: The highest mountain in the Americas, located in the Andes mountain range.

wiki.extract: Aconcagua is a mountain in the Principal Cordillera of the Andes range, located in Mendoza Province, Argentina. With a summit elevation of 6,967.15 metres, it is the highest mountain in the Americas, the highest outside Asia, and the highest peak in both the Western and Southern Hemispheres. It is the second-most topographically prominent peak in the world and one of the Seven Summits, the highest mountains on each of the seven continents.

cultural_events.name: Carnaval
cultural_events.writeup: A lively festival celebrated with parades, music, and dancing, especially vibrant in the northern provinces.

wiki.extract: Carnival is a festive season at the close of the Christian pre-Lenten period, consisting of Quinquagesima or Shrove Sunday, Shrove Monday, and Shrove Tuesday or Mardi Gras.

cultural_events.name: Tango Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event in Buenos Aires celebrating the traditional Argentine dance and music.

wiki.extract: Argentine tango is a musical genre and accompanying social dance originating at the end of the 19th century in the suburbs of Buenos Aires. It typically has a 24 or 44 rhythmic time signature, and two or three parts repeating in patterns such as ABAB or ABCAC. Its lyrics are marked by nostalgia, sadness, and laments for lost love. The typical orchestra has several melodic instruments and is given a distinctive air by the bandoneon. It has continued to grow in popularity and spread internationally, adding modern elements without replacing the older ones. Among its leading figures are the singer and songwriter Carlos Gardel and composers/performers Francisco Canaro, Juan D'Arienzo, Carlos Di Sarli, Osvaldo Pugliese, Elvira Santamaría, and Ástor Piazzolla.

cultural_events.name: Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia
cultural_events.writeup: The National Grape Harvest Festival held in Mendoza, celebrating the wine harvest with parades and performances.

wiki.extract: Fiesta Nacional de la Vendimia takes place annually in Mendoza City, Argentina. It is one of the most important festivals in the country, attracting large numbers of tourists to the region. It is a celebration of wine and the winemaking industry.

food_writeup: Argentine cuisine is renowned for its beef, particularly asado (barbecue), empanadas, and mate, a traditional herbal tea. Italian and Spanish influences are prominent in the culinary landscape.
brief_history: Argentina declared independence from Spain in 1816. It experienced periods of economic growth and political instability throughout the 19th and 20th centuries, including military dictatorships and democratic transitions. Today, it is a federal republic with a diverse cultural heritage.

important_people.name: Eva Perón
important_people.description: Influential political figure and First Lady

current_conflicts: Argentina has no active armed conflicts but faces ongoing economic challenges and territorial disputes, notably over the Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas) with the United Kingdom.

main_events.headline: Pulp mill dispute with Uruguay escalates
main_events.summary: Argentina takes Uruguay to the International Court of Justice over mills on the shared river as bridge blockades continue.

main_events.headline: Dictatorship-trial witness disappears
main_events.summary: Julio López vanishes in September after testifying against a former police chief, sparking national outrage and a fruitless search.

sport.headline: World Cup quarter-final exit to Germany
sport.summary: Argentina loses on penalties in Berlin; coach José Pekerman resigns after the defeat.

main_events.headline: Cristina Kirchner elected president
main_events.summary: She wins October's vote to succeed her husband Néstor, becoming Argentina's first elected woman president.

main_events.headline: Cash-smuggling scandal strains Venezuela ties
main_events.summary: The Antonini Wilson suitcase case links Venezuelan funds to the Kirchner campaign, embarrassing both governments.

sport.headline: Copa América final defeat to Brazil
sport.summary: Argentina loses 3-0 in Venezuela, but the under-20s win the World Cup with Sergio Agüero starring.

main_events.headline: Farm export-tax revolt paralyzes government
main_events.summary: Four months of farmer strikes over Resolution 125 end when the Senate rejects the mobile export-tax hike.

main_events.headline: Government seizes private pension funds
main_events.summary: Cristina nationalizes the AFJP pension system in November, citing the global financial crisis.

sport.headline: Olympic football gold in Beijing
sport.summary: Messi and Agüero lead Argentina to a second straight Olympic title, beating Nigeria in the final.

main_events.headline: Kirchnerism routed in midterm elections
main_events.summary: The government's list loses Buenos Aires province in June, weakening Cristina ahead of the 2011 race.

main_events.headline: Media law battle with Clarín begins
main_events.summary: Congress passes a law to break up the Clarín group, opening a years-long legal and political war.

sport.headline: Last-gasp World Cup qualification
sport.summary: Palermo's late winner against Peru and victory in Uruguay seal qualification under coach Maradona.

main_events.headline: Néstor Kirchner dies suddenly
main_events.summary: The former president dies of a heart attack in October, reshaping Cristina's government and the 2011 race.

main_events.headline: Same-sex marriage legalized
main_events.summary: Argentina becomes the first Latin American country to legalize gay marriage in July.

sport.headline: World Cup quarter-final humiliation by Germany
sport.summary: A 4-0 defeat in Cape Town ends Maradona's coaching reign; Messi leaves the tournament scoreless.

main_events.headline: Cristina re-elected in landslide
main_events.summary: She wins 54 percent in October's first round, the widest margin since the return of democracy.

main_events.headline: Currency controls introduced
main_events.summary: 'Cepo' restrictions on dollar purchases begin as capital flight accelerates.

sport.headline: Copa América flop on home soil
sport.summary: Argentina exits in the quarter-finals to Uruguay on penalties despite hosting the tournament.

main_events.headline: YPF renationalized from Spain's Repsol
main_events.summary: Congress expropriates a 51 percent stake in April, triggering a diplomatic row with Madrid.

main_events.headline: Mass cacerolazo protests erupt
main_events.summary: Hundreds of thousands march in November against inflation, crime and corruption.

sport.headline: Messi scores record 91 goals in a year
sport.summary: He breaks Gerd Müller's 40-year record in December, capping a historic Barcelona season.

main_events.headline: IMF censures Argentina over inflation data
main_events.summary: The Fund issues a rare censure in February over doctored official statistics.

main_events.headline: Argentine cardinal becomes Pope Francis
main_events.summary: Jorge Bergoglio's March election thrills the country; Cristina attends the inauguration.

sport.headline: World Cup qualification sealed top of group
sport.summary: Argentina books Brazil 2014 with games to spare as Messi stars in qualifying.

main_events.headline: Default on holdout 'vulture fund' debt
main_events.summary: Argentina defaults in July after US courts block payments unless holdout creditors are paid in full.

main_events.headline: Peso sharply devalued
main_events.summary: The government lets the peso slide in January as foreign reserves drain.

sport.headline: World Cup final heartbreak against Germany
sport.summary: Götze's extra-time goal in Rio denies Argentina a third title; Messi wins the Golden Ball.

main_events.headline: Prosecutor Nisman found dead
main_events.summary: Alberto Nisman is found shot in January, days before testifying that Cristina covered up the AMIA bombing probe.

main_events.headline: Macri ends 12 years of Kirchnerism
main_events.summary: Mauricio Macri beats Daniel Scioli in November's runoff, the country's first ever presidential ballotage.

sport.headline: Copa América final loss to Chile
sport.summary: Argentina falls on penalties in Santiago; Messi misses in the shootout.

main_events.headline: Argentina settles with holdout creditors
main_events.summary: Macri's government pays billions to end the 15-year debt saga and returns to bond markets.

main_events.headline: 'Panama Papers' implicate Macri
main_events.summary: Leaked documents link the president to offshore firms, though he denies wrongdoing.

sport.headline: Copa América final defeat prompts Messi retirement
sport.summary: A third straight final loss, again to Chile on penalties, leads Messi to briefly quit the national team.

main_events.headline: Activist Maldonado found dead
main_events.summary: Santiago Maldonado's body is found in October after a 78-day disappearance that polarized the country.

main_events.headline: Macri wins midterm elections
main_events.summary: Cambiemos triumphs nationally in October, strengthening the reform agenda.

sport.headline: Messi hat-trick rescues World Cup qualification
sport.summary: His three goals in Quito against Ecuador seal a last-day ticket to Russia 2018.

main_events.headline: Record $57bn IMF bailout agreed
main_events.summary: A peso collapse forces Macri to seek the largest loan in IMF history in June.

main_events.headline: Buenos Aires hosts G20 summit
main_events.summary: Trump, Putin and Xi attend the November summit amid tight security.

sport.headline: World Cup last-16 exit to France
sport.summary: A 4-3 thriller in Kazan ends Argentina's campaign; coach Sampaoli departs.

main_events.headline: Fernández defeats Macri
main_events.summary: Alberto Fernández, with Cristina as running mate, wins October's election on economic discontent.

main_events.headline: Markets crash after primary shock
main_events.summary: The peso and stocks plunge in August when Fernández trounces Macri in the PASO primary.

sport.headline: Copa América semi-final loss to Brazil
sport.summary: A 2-0 defeat in Belo Horizonte ends the title bid; Messi alleges corruption in officiating.

main_events.headline: Sovereign debt restructured
main_events.summary: After months of talks, Argentina seals a $65bn bond restructuring deal in August.

main_events.headline: Abortion legalized
main_events.summary: Congress legalizes abortion up to 14 weeks in December after a historic feminist campaign.

sport.headline: Maradona dies aged 60
sport.summary: The nation's idol dies of a heart attack in November; three days of national mourning are declared.

main_events.headline: 'VIP vaccination' scandal topples minister
main_events.summary: Health minister Ginés González García resigns in February over preferential vaccine access.

main_events.headline: Government crushed in midterms
main_events.summary: The ruling coalition loses control of Congress in November amid soaring inflation.

sport.headline: Copa América triumph at the Maracanã
sport.summary: Di María's goal beats Brazil 1-0 in the final, ending a 28-year trophy drought.

main_events.headline: Vice president survives assassination attempt
main_events.summary: Cristina Kirchner is attacked at point-blank range in September; the gun misfires.

main_events.headline: Inflation nears 100 percent
main_events.summary: Annual inflation hits about 95 percent in December as the economy unravels.

sport.headline: World Cup champions in Qatar
sport.summary: Argentina beats France on penalties in a classic final; Messi finally lifts the trophy.

main_events.headline: Milei wins presidency
main_events.summary: Libertarian outsider Javier Milei beats Sergio Massa in November's runoff on a radical free-market platform.

main_events.headline: Primary shock rattles markets
main_events.summary: Milei's surprise PASO win in August sends the peso tumbling and inflation soaring.

sport.headline: Messi joins Inter Miami
sport.summary: After leaving PSG, the World Cup winner moves to MLS in a landmark July transfer.

main_events.headline: Milei achieves fiscal surplus
main_events.summary: Drastic spending cuts deliver monthly budget surpluses, though poverty spikes above 50 percent.

main_events.headline: 'Ley Bases' reform package passes
main_events.summary: Congress approves Milei's sweeping deregulation bill in June after months of protests.

sport.headline: Copa América title retained
sport.summary: Lautaro Martínez's extra-time goal beats Colombia in the Miami final for a record 16th title.

main_events.headline: '$LIBRA' crypto scandal engulfs Milei
main_events.summary: The president promotes a memecoin in February that collapses within hours, sparking fraud probes.

main_events.headline: Milei's party wins midterms
main_events.summary: La Libertad Avanza triumphs in October's legislative elections, consolidating power in Congress.

sport.headline: World Cup 2026 qualification secured
sport.summary: Argentina becomes the first South American team to book its ticket, sealing it in March.
